answer: On a wide meadow at dawn, keepers run a mirror relay: one opal lens on the hilltop catches first light and each keeper angles one mirror to pass the beam to the next post. Each morning a second keeper walks the line, checks the beam lands inside a chalk ring at the far end, and signs the reading. A dusty mirror or one tilted a finger width breaks the chain, so a copied identity earns nothing without its own polished glass and walk. A thousand fake names need a thousand clean mirrors and a thousand dawn walks, while one honest keeper tends one mirror.
